question: Should video time read in frames (timecode) everywhere, or stay in seconds with timecode as a choice in the View menu?
context: Reproduced at Next defaults on 2026-10-02: the transport reads 0:04, the ruler at its closest zoom counts 3.9s, 4s, 4.1s, and a transition's length bubble and panel Length both say 0.8s. Nothing shows frames. The mocks draw seconds everywhere, so showing frames by default would be a departure from them.

options.label: Timecode everywhere
options.summary: Every time on a video reads like Premiere: the transport says 00:00:04:12, the ruler counts timecode and shows a tick per frame up close, and a transition you drag says 00:00:00:24 in its bubble and its Length row.
pros: An editor can land on a frame they can name, with nothing to switch on
One way of reading time across the whole window
cons: Long numbers where today there are short ones (0:04 becomes 00:00:04:00)
Goes against the video mocks, which draw seconds throughout
Harder going for someone trimming a screen recording who has never heard of frames
options.mitigation: Lengths can read short, as 24f in the bubble and the Length row, so only a position on the clock carries the full timecode.

options.label: Seconds, with Timecode in the View menu
options.summary: Today's seconds stay the default, as the mocks draw them. View, then Time Display, offers Seconds or Timecode, and picking Timecode turns every readout over at once. In both, a drag lands on a whole frame and a length box takes 12f or 00:00:00:12.
pros: Keeps the mocks' look for people who think in seconds
Matches Premiere, which also lets you pick how time is shown
Transport, ruler, bubble and panel always agree to the frame, whichever you pick
cons: An editor has to find the setting once before frames show
options.mitigation: The choice is remembered across documents and launches, so it is set once.

options.label: Leave time in seconds
options.summary: Nothing visible changes: time keeps reading 0:04, 3.9s and 0.8s, and frames stay out of sight.
pros: No new setting and no long numbers
cons: An editor still cannot land on a frame they can name, which is the gap this task was filed for
options.mitigation: Seconds with hundredths at the closest zoom already gets within a frame or two.
